  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header of the maamar for Shabbos Mattos-Masei, Menachem Av 5713.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B'S"D.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Mattos-Masei,</t>
    <t s="2">Rosh Chodesh Menachem-Av*,</t>
    <t s="3">the year 5713</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that the text is an unedited transcription.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(An unedited transcription)</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verse and raises several textual difficulties regarding the plural language, Moshe's writing, and the repetition of "their departures" and "their journeys."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"These are the journeys of the children of Israel who went out of the land of Egypt... and Moshe wrote their departures according to their journeys... and these are their journeys according to their departures."</t>
    <t s="1">And the precise points</t>
    <t s="2">in this are known,</t>
    <t s="3">[namely] that it says "These are the journeys,"</t>
    <t s="4">which is in the plural,</t>
    <t s="5">and it concludes "who went out of the land of Egypt," which is only the first departure and journey.</t>
    <t s="6">Also, the statement "and Moshe wrote" is not understood,</t>
    <t s="7">for Moshe Rabbeinu wrote the entire Torah,</t>
    <t s="8">so what does this inform us?</t>
    <t s="9">Also, what is the repetition of "their departures according to their journeys" and "their journeys according to their departures,"</t>
    <t s="10">and the reversal of order from the beginning to the end?</t>
    <t s="11">And in general, one must understand,</t>
    <t s="12">what is the relevance of the narrative and knowledge of the order of the journeys,</t>
    <t s="13">and even for that generation, the Midrash explains</t>
    <t s="14">a parable of a king and his son who traveled... when they returned they would count all the journeys and events that occurred in them,</t>
    <t s="15">but the Torah is eternal,</t>
    <t s="16">and therefore this narrative is relevant in all times and in all places.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
